title: The Car Engine
objective: After this level you can explain how a four-stroke engine turns fuel into motion.
summary: A car engine burns fuel inside its cylinders. Intake, compression, power, exhaust: one push per cycle, and only about 12%-30% of the fuel energy moves the car.

cards.headline: Only about 12%-30% of the energy in a gas tank moves the car.
cards.body: Most of the rest is lost in the engine, mainly as heat. That sounds wasteful, and it is, but the engine still gets the job done. Here's how it turns fuel into motion, one burst of hot gas at a time.

cards.headline: Fire inside the cylinder
cards.body: Level 22's steam engines made their steam in a separate boiler, then piped it to the piston. A car engine is an internal combustion engine: the fuel burns inside the cylinder itself. A spark plug ignites a mix of gasoline and air, and the hot, expanding gas shoves the piston. No boiler, no waiting for water to boil.

events.label: The piston moves down, drawing in fuel and air
The piston moves up, squeezing the mix
A spark ignites it; expanding gas drives the piston down
The piston moves up, pushing the burned gases out

cards.fact: Only one stroke in four actually pushes.
cards.context: A connecting rod links the piston to a crankshaft, which turns the up-and-down motion into spinning, much as your legs turn a bike's pedals. Each four-stroke cycle takes two turns of the crankshaft. Nikolaus Otto built an engine on this idea in 1876, though a Frenchman, Alphonse Beau de Rochas, had patented the cycle first.

questions.prompt: In a four-stroke car engine, which stroke drives the piston to do the work?

options.label: Intake
options.rationale: That stroke draws in fuel and air.

options.label: Exhaust
options.rationale: That stroke clears out the burned gases.

questions.explanation: In the power stroke a spark ignites the squeezed mix, and the expanding gas drives the piston down.

questions.prompt: What makes a car engine an internal combustion engine?

options.label: Its fuel burns inside the cylinder
It boils water in a boiler first
options.rationale: That is how a steam engine works.

questions.prompt: Level 2 said energy is never destroyed. So where does most of a gas car's fuel energy go?

options.label: It is destroyed by the spark plug
It is stored in the crankshaft
options.rationale: A crankshaft turns; it does not store the fuel's energy.
